answer: Sybil resistance means making each fake agent expensive to run and cheap to expose. Here, an agent is a graph vertex admitted only after posting escrow, so an attacker must stake real funds per identity instead of spawning them for free. The resulting cluster looks solid but is hollow inside: no earned trust, no signature history. Any peer on that ledge can submit proof of duplicate behavior, and slashing pays the challenger. Creating n sybils then costs n stakes plus a bounty, so flooding the economy is structurally unprofitable.
